name: Atlas
subtitle: Portfolio Intelligence Agent
headline: The AI behind the chat widget on this portfolio. Type to it, talk to it, or meet it face to face.
description: Atlas answers questions about Gaurav in real time, by text, by voice, or as a live video avatar. It runs on Google's Agent Development Kit, calling live retrieval tools that fetch his profile, work history, projects, certifications, and recent writing straight from the site on every question, so content edits show up with no redeploy. Four Gemini models sit behind it: a dedicated speech model for the mic, a tiered reasoning cascade for the answer, a TTS model that reads the reply back while it is still streaming, and Gemini Live Avatar, which speaks the answer as lip-synced video.
value: Handles inbound career questions 24/7 without Gaurav being online. Every answer cites its source. Visitors can talk to it instead of typing, have it talk back, or switch to Avatar mode and hear the answer from a live, lip-synced video avatar. When a visitor asks to send a resume or drop Gaurav a note, the agent calls an email tool via MCP and makes it happen.
diagramAlt: Browser mic, speaker, composer and avatar stage talk to Atlas on Cloud Run. The mic and speaker use two plain REST routes that call Gemini 3.5 Transcribe and Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS on Vertex AI directly. The composer streams over SSE to the ADK Agent, which reasons on Gemini 3.6 Flash with a 3.5 Flash-Lite fallback, calls retrieval tools and the Resend MCP server, and passes every answer through output checks. In Avatar mode a relay on the same route sends the checked answer to Gemini 3.8 Live Avatar and streams the lip-synced video and timed words back on the same SSE stream to the browser's avatar stage. Text, Voice and Avatar are alternative paths back, chosen before the question is asked.

steps.label: Optionally, the visitor holds the mic and speaks (any mode)
steps.detail: MediaRecorder captures a clip in the browser, capped at 30 seconds, and posts it to /api/agent-transcribe. Nothing reaches a model until the visitor stops recording.

steps.label: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe returns a clean transcript
steps.detail: A purpose-built speech model, not a reasoning model with audio bolted on. SMART mode strips filler words and false starts, and a custom vocabulary biases recognition toward the proper nouns on this site. The transcript prefills the composer and stops there. A human keystroke always sends the message.

steps.label: The message opens an SSE stream
steps.detail: The browser opens a Server-Sent Events stream to /api/agent-chat on Cloud Run. Questions are rate-limited per session and per IP, and stripped of injection attempts before reaching the ADK runner. The visitor picked Text, Voice or Avatar before asking, and that choice sets the answer's way back. In Avatar mode the same request also opens a Gemini 3.8 Live Avatar session in parallel, so the face is live and idling while Atlas thinks.

steps.label: The agent reasons and calls the tool it needs
steps.detail: Gemini picks from nine on-demand tools, covering profile, work history, projects, posts, certifications, live agents, site stats, and two email actions, instead of stuffing the whole corpus into every prompt. Retrieval tools read the site's own content JSON at request time. Email actions route through the Resend MCP server, so the agent holds no credentials. Inference starts on gemini-3.6-flash, picked for time to first word, and moves to gemini-3.5-flash-lite if it stalls or hits a capacity error.

steps.label: Output checks clean every answer on its way out
steps.detail: Before anything reaches the screen, the stream passes filters written in code rather than prompt rules: the working note moves to the Thinking panel, any email address that isn't Gaurav's real contact is replaced, combined citation markers are split, and dashes become commas. Spoken modes are asked for a shorter answer, sized for listening. An end-to-end scorecard that caught an invented email and invented platform work is why these live in code.

steps.label: The answer streams back with citations. In Text mode, that is the whole trip
steps.detail: Tokens stream through SSE as they are generated. A [[META]] block carries citation URLs and follow-up chip suggestions, which the widget validates and renders as UI. In Avatar mode the same stream also carries the video and the timed words.

steps.label: Voice mode: the browser cuts the reply into sentences and sends them to be spoken
steps.detail: If the visitor has turned on spoken replies, the widget splits the stream at sentence boundaries and posts each chunk to /api/agent-speak while the rest of the answer is still arriving. Chunk sizes ramp up, so the first words start playing after the first short sentence rather than after the whole answer.

steps.label: Voice mode: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS returns audio, Web Audio plays it seamlessly
steps.detail: Each chunk comes back as 24 kHz PCM in the Charon voice. The browser decodes it and schedules it on the Web Audio clock at the exact moment the previous chunk ends, so there is no gap between sentences. Up to two syntheses run ahead of playback to keep it that way.

steps.label: Avatar mode: the checked answer becomes the avatar's script
steps.detail: A relay on the chat route sends the finished, checked answer into the Live Avatar session opened back at step 3 as a script. Sam, a prebuilt avatar with the Puck voice, says it word for word about a second later. Caps keep it affordable: three avatar answers per visitor a day, and a daily speaking budget.

steps.label: Avatar mode: lip-synced video and timed words stream back on the same SSE
steps.detail: The avatar's fMP4 video fragments and its speech transcription come back through the relay onto the chat's own stream, so the browser needs no second connection. The server reads each fragment's media time and stamps every caption chunk with when its last word is heard. The browser plays the video through MediaSource and lights each word of the transcript as Sam says it.

techDecisions.why: Structured Python framework for tools, evals, and Cloud Run deployment. An eval gate runs before every deploy, catching regressions before production.

3.6 Flash was picked for time to first word: the end-to-end scorecard measures a median of about 3 seconds to the first word, at a fraction of Pro's cost. If it stalls for 4 seconds or hits a capacity error, the request moves to 3.5 Flash-Lite on Vertex AI, so the widget keeps answering instead of erroring when one model is briefly unavailable.

techDecisions.tech: A dedicated speech model, not Flash with audio
techDecisions.why: Gemini Flash can transcribe audio, but it decides what to keep as a byproduct of reasoning. gemini-3.5-transcribe has two switches a reasoning model does not: SMART mode, which strips filler words and self-corrections, and a custom vocabulary that biases recognition toward names like Deloitte, Topmate, and ADK. Both matter more here than raw capability.

techDecisions.tech: Voice runs as plain REST, outside the ADK loop
techDecisions.why: The transcribe and speak routes call Vertex directly instead of going through the agent. The text path is untouched, so if speech fails the answer is still on screen. They also spend their own rate-limit budgets, which means a bad recording or a long spoken reply never costs a visitor one of their ten questions.

techDecisions.tech: Sentence-chunked TTS on the Web Audio clock
techDecisions.why: Synthesising a whole answer means waiting for the whole answer. Instead the reply is cut at sentence boundaries as it streams, chunks are synthesised up to two ahead in parallel, and each is scheduled back to back on the AudioContext clock so playback has no seams. Synthesis runs at roughly 0.7x realtime, so once it starts it stays ahead.

techDecisions.tech: Gemini 3.8 Live Avatar, through a server relay
techDecisions.why: Live Avatar is server-to-server only, so the browser never holds a key or talks to it directly. The chat request opens the avatar session in parallel with the agent, which hides most of the session setup behind the thinking time, and the server only ever speaks the answer it just generated, so nobody can make the face say arbitrary text. Per-visitor and daily caps keep the cost bounded.

techDecisions.tech: Output checks in code, not prompt rules
techDecisions.why: Prompt rules reduce mistakes; they don't prevent them. An end-to-end scorecard caught Atlas inventing a work email and inventing platform experience from a certification, even with rules against both. So the stream now passes filters that can't be talked around: contact emails, citation markers, dashes and the working note are all enforced in code, and certifications carry whether any real work backs them.

techDecisions.tech: Word timing from the video itself
techDecisions.why: The avatar's transcription arrives ahead of its audio by a steady margin, and the browser can't see how much video it has actually received. So the server reads each fMP4 fragment's media time and stamps every caption chunk with when its last word is heard, calibrated against the real pauses in a recorded answer. The transcript lights one word at a time, in step with the voice.

The corpus is exposed as on-demand tools reading the live site content, not a per-turn full-corpus dump or a frozen deploy-time snapshot. The model calls only the tool it needs, cutting prompt tokens while staying current with content edits.

The first attempt was zero idle cost plus a scheduled ping to keep an instance warm. That kept failing in practice, so it now runs a permanent minimum instance for a few dollars a month. Cold starts became structurally impossible instead of merely unlikely, and the cheaper option was tried honestly first.
Decouples email from the agent binary. The Resend MCP Server is a separate Cloud Run service, reused by the Ambient Agent, making it a shared capability.
Simpler than WebSockets for one-way streaming: no upgrade handshake, works through CDN, natively supported by the browser fetch API.

traits.label: Pattern
traits.value: Tool Use · MCP · Streaming · Voice · Avatar

evidence.text: Streams answers in the chat widget and cites the page each one came from.
evidence.voice: Hears you through Gemini 3.5 Transcribe and answers out loud with Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS.
evidence.avatar: Talks back on camera through Gemini 3.8 Live Avatar, lip-synced, with word-timed captions.
evidence.ondemand: Wakes the moment a visitor opens the chat or starts a call, and answers in real time.
evidence.cites: Live tools fetch Gaurav's profile, projects and posts, so every answer comes from the site itself.
evidence.acts: Emails the resume or a note to Gaurav through the Resend MCP server, once you confirm the address.

name: Pulse
subtitle: Ambient Agent
headline: The autonomous agent running silently behind this portfolio.
description: Pulse is a scheduled, background agent. Cloud Scheduler fires it twice a week. It fetches visitor interaction stats from Cloudflare D1, identifies engagement patterns, drafts personalised follow-up notes for qualifying leads, and emails a digest, all without Gaurav initiating anything.
value: Turns passive visitor data into actionable outreach while Gaurav sleeps. Every run completes in under 30 seconds, leaves an audit trail, and only sends email when engagement thresholds are met.
diagramAlt: Cloud Scheduler → Ambient Agent (ADK/Gemini) → Cloudflare D1 (stats) + Resend MCP (email)

steps.label: Cloud Scheduler fires the trigger
steps.detail: An authenticated POST hits /api/ambient/run on Cloud Run every Monday and Thursday at 08:00 IST. The bearer token is validated before handing off to the ADK runner.

steps.label: Agent fetches visitor interaction stats
steps.detail: get_recent_interactions calls the Cloudflare Worker, which reads agent_interactions and page_views from D1. The agent receives the last 4 days of chat turns and page views.

steps.label: Insights generated, leads qualified
steps.detail: Gemini 3.8 Flash reasons over the interaction data: top questions, resume downloads, hiring-intent signals. Leads above the threshold get a draft outreach note.

steps.label: Digest email sent to Gaurav via MCP
steps.detail: The agent calls the Resend MCP Server with a weekly summary: engagement stats, top questions, notable visitors. Always sent, regardless of lead count.

techDecisions.why: Managed cron, zero infrastructure. Integrates with Cloud Run via OIDC natively. Mon/Thu cadence gives a 3–4 day window of interaction data per run.
Runs as a standalone Agent with no session state; starts fresh each run, completes cleanly. Same ADK version as the chat agent; single Cloud Run service.
Interaction data already lives in D1 via the Cloudflare Worker analytics backend. Reusing it avoids a second database; 90-day row expiry keeps the table lean.
Same MCP server used by Atlas handles email here. One credential to rotate, one audit log; sharing was trivial because both agents just call the same endpoint.
Pulse runs as a separate service from Atlas, so a digest run never competes with a visitor's chat, and each one deploys and scales on its own.

evidence.autonomous: Cloud Scheduler wakes it every Monday and Thursday. Nobody has to be watching.
evidence.acts: Pulls visitor stats from Cloudflare D1 and emails Gaurav a digest through MCP.

name: ErrorLens
subtitle: Self-learning GCP error resolution system
headline: Diagnoses GCP errors and gets smarter with every confirmed fix.
description: ErrorLens is a multi-agent orchestrator that triages GCP errors, runs parallel research across documentation and community sources, and stores confirmed resolutions in a vector knowledge bank. Mature deployments skip the research pipeline entirely for previously encountered issues via semantic similarity matching (≥0.85 threshold).
value: Reduces mean-time-to-resolution for recurring GCP errors by accumulating institutional knowledge across every incident. The self-improving feedback loop means the system delivers faster, higher-confidence answers over time.
diagramAlt: ErrorLens multi-agent architecture: orchestrator routes errors to quick-scan or full research pipeline, with A2A KB agent backed by AlloyDB vector store

steps.label: Error intake
steps.detail: Developer submits a GCP error. The orchestrator determines if a known fix exists in the knowledge bank.

steps.label: Quick scan
steps.detail: Sequential signal extraction + KB vector search (≥0.85 similarity). Returns immediately if a match is found.

steps.label: Sage pipeline
steps.detail: For novel errors: deep_search runs GCP docs and community agents in parallel, then aggregates with composite confidence scoring.

steps.label: Parallel research
steps.detail: GCP Knowledge Agent and Community Search Agent run concurrently, searching official docs and Stack Overflow / GitHub Issues.

steps.label: External research
steps.detail: GCP Knowledge Agent calls a managed MCP server for official GCP docs; Community Search Agent uses Google Search for SO, Reddit and GitHub issues, and both run in parallel. On KB HIT, quick_scan bypasses sage_pipeline via a direct hot-path into the KB Toolbox.

steps.label: A2A KB record
steps.detail: Confirmed fixes are dispatched to error-kb-agent via A2A Protocol, triggering embedding regeneration to include the resolution.

steps.label: MCP tool execution
steps.detail: error-kb-agent calls error-kb-toolbox (MCP Toolbox for Databases) to read/write cases, perform vector searches, and deposit fixes.

steps.label: AlloyDB pgvector
steps.detail: 768-dimensional embeddings from Vertex AI text-embedding-005 power semantic similarity search across the growing case library.

steps.label: PDF export
steps.detail: The orchestrator generates a structured PDF diagnostic report delivered back to the developer.

techDecisions.why: Enables error-kb-agent to be independently deployed and versioned on Cloud Run while remaining callable from the main orchestrator over HTTP.
PostgreSQL-compatible vector store with native pgvector extension and Vertex AI integration for high-quality 768-dim embeddings, so no separate vector DB is needed.
Decouples SQL/vector logic from agent code; exposes database operations as typed MCP tools consumable by any ADK agent.
GCP docs and community sources are searched concurrently via ParallelAgent, cutting research latency roughly in half.

evidence.ondemand: Runs when a developer submits a GCP error, then works it through to a fix.
evidence.team: An orchestrator sends each error to a quick scan or a parallel research pipeline, with a knowledge agent over A2A.
evidence.cites: Searches GCP docs and community sources, plus its own vector knowledge bank in AlloyDB.
evidence.acts: Writes confirmed fixes to AlloyDB and queries it through the MCP Toolbox for Databases.
evidence.learns: Every confirmed fix is remembered, so the next time that error shows up it skips the research.

name: Agentic RAG
subtitle: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipeline
headline: An 8-stage agentic RAG pipeline, rendered as a 3D vector space you can step through.
description: Agentic RAG runs the full 8-stage RAG pipeline as a FastAPI service on Cloud Run and renders every stage as an interactive 3D vector space. Ingest any document via text paste, PDF/file upload, URL fetch, or image (Gemini Vision extracts text first). Choose your embedding model, Voyage AI voyage-3 (1024-D) or Gemini Embedding 2 (3072-D), and watch each chunk fly into the vector space. On query, dual retrieval runs cosine search over ChromaDB and BM25 keyword scan in parallel, Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges the rankings, and the answer is grounded strictly in the retrieved chunks, with no training knowledge. Supports Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 3.5 Flash as generation models.
value: Makes the invisible parts of RAG legible: you watch chunks become vectors, see why nearest neighbours win on cosine distance, and how lexical and semantic retrieval disagree before RRF reconciles them. A relevance gate blocks off-topic queries (cosine < 0.45) so the model never hallucinates from training knowledge. The Agentic/Linear toggle shows the difference between a one-shot pipeline and a reasoning loop where the LLM calls hybrid_search on demand.
diagramAlt: 8-stage agentic RAG pipeline on Cloud Run: chunk → generate embedding (Voyage) → store in vector DB (ChromaDB) → embed query → retrieve (dense + BM25) → RRF fusion → augment → grounded answer (Claude), with an agentic tool-use loop from generation back to retrieval, streamed to the browser over SSE

steps.label: Chunk the document
steps.detail: Accepts text paste, PDF/file upload, URL (server-side HTML extraction strips nav and boilerplate), or image (Gemini Vision converts the image to text first). The document is then split by a recursive character splitter (800 chars / 120 overlap) across four strategies: recursive, sentence, paragraph, or fixed-window. The 3D view shows chunk boundaries laid over the source text.

steps.label: Generate embeddings
steps.detail: Each chunk is sent to the chosen embedding model, Voyage AI voyage-3 (1024-D) or Gemini Embedding 2 (3072-D), and returned as a high-dimensional vector. PCA then reduces those vectors to three principal components so the corpus can fly into the 3D scene with explained-variance labels on each axis.

steps.label: Store in the vector DB
steps.detail: Vectors are written to a ChromaDB collection over cosine space, and the points populate the 3D vector space one at a time. A parallel BM25 index is built over the same chunks for lexical retrieval.

steps.label: Embed the query
steps.detail: On query, the question is embedded by the same model into the same PCA basis, so it lands in the same space as the chunks. The query point drops into the 3D scene alongside the corpus.

steps.label: Retrieve: dense + lexical
steps.detail: The query runs through both a dense cosine search over ChromaDB and a BM25 keyword scan, side by side. Cosine similarity to every chunk is surfaced as a live distance table over the 3D canvas, with connection lines to the nearest neighbours.

steps.label: Fuse with RRF
steps.detail: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60) blends the semantic and lexical rankings into one final top-k set. Because RRF only cares about rank position, it merges the two scorers without needing them to share a scale, reconciling cases where keyword overlap and vector proximity disagree.

steps.label: Augment the prompt
steps.detail: The fused chunks are assembled into numbered, citable passages and injected into the LLM prompt as grounded context. The token estimate and chunk indices are shown so the cost and provenance of the context are explicit.

steps.label: Grounded answer (agentic loop)
steps.detail: Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, or Gemini 3.5 Flash streams an answer grounded strictly in the retrieved chunks. A strict system prompt blocks training-knowledge fallback. Off-topic queries (cosine similarity below 0.45) are blocked before generation. In agentic mode the LLM holds a hybrid_search tool and re-queries on demand, turning a linear pipeline into a reasoning loop.

techDecisions.why: The pipeline ships as a single FastAPI service on Cloud Run (min-instances=0, zero idle cost). Server-Sent Events stream chunks, vectors, retrieval results, and answer tokens over one channel with no WebSocket handshake, so the 3D view updates live as each stage completes.

Two embedding models are supported: Voyage voyage-3 (1024-D, best for text) and Gemini Embedding 2 (3072-D, required for image inputs since Voyage is text-only). Images are first converted to text via Gemini Vision, then embedded. Keys are resolved per model (Voyage/Anthropic key for Voyage, Google key for Gemini) and never stored server-side.
Dense vector search alone misses exact-keyword matches; BM25 alone misses paraphrase. Running both and fusing teaches why production RAG is almost always hybrid, not purely semantic.
RRF blends rankings without needing the two scorers to share a scale. It only cares about rank position. Simple, robust, and the standard way to merge dense and sparse retrieval.

Projecting 1024-D embeddings to three principal components makes the vector space visible and orbit-able. The explained-variance labels on each axis keep the lossy reduction honest about what's being shown.

Linear RAG retrieves once; agentic RAG lets Claude call hybrid_search on demand and re-query when the first pass is thin. The Agentic/Linear toggle makes the difference between a pipeline and an agent tangible.

evidence.ondemand: Runs each time you ingest a document or ask a question, and streams every stage live.
evidence.cites: Runs dense and BM25 search side by side, fuses them with RRF, and answers only from what it found.
